title: FX Brief — 18 Nov 2026
intro: Risk aversion dominates the European session as equities slide and geopolitical tensions escalate in the Gulf alongside widespread infrastructure outages. The US dollar gains ground with DXY up 0.29 percent to 103.79, while safe-haven flows and risk-off sentiment dictate broader currency dynamics.

sections.heading: FX theme
sections.content: Geopolitical risk and macro uncertainty drive today's FX markets, compounded by heavy central bank speaker schedules and upcoming FOMC minutes. Safe-haven currencies lead the daily strength ranking while commodity currencies lag amid falling oil and gold prices.

sections.heading: Dollar read
sections.content: The US dollar strengthens across the board as the DXY rises to 103.79, supported by a slight retreat in US 10-year yields down 1.8 basis points to 5.103 percent. Commodity currencies like AUD/USD and NZD/USD suffer from declining risk appetite, while USD/CHF gains 0.19 percent to 0.8414.

sections.heading: Crosses
sections.content: Yen crosses decline across the board, led by EUR/JPY down 0.39 percent to 174.758 and AUD/JPY down 0.32 percent to 107.120, reflecting acute risk aversion. Euro crosses also edge lower as EUR/USD drops 0.20 percent to 1.0976 and EUR/GBP slips 0.11 percent to 0.8332.

sections.heading: Potential scenarios
sections.content:
- *▲ Bullish · DXY — above 104.00 opens 105.00 · invalid below 103.50*
Broad safe-haven demand pushes the dollar higher amid escalating Gulf tensions and global outages.
- *▼ Bearish · EUR/USD — below 1.0950 opens 1.0820 · invalid above 1.1010*
Weaker euro performance and persistent dollar strength weigh on the pair below parity pressures.
- *▼ Bearish · USD/JPY — below 158.800 opens 156.500 · invalid above 159.800*
- *▼ Bearish · AUD/USD — below 0.6700 opens 0.6550 · invalid above 0.6760*
Softer Australian wage data and declining commodity prices pressure the Australian dollar.

sections.heading: Key risks
sections.content:
- Escalation of military conflict in the Gulf region affecting energy supplies and global risk sentiment.
- Unanticipated hawkish signals from upcoming Federal Reserve meeting minutes and central bank speeches.
